notes: Dev ABox revision on cell_kind (functional). The edit puts yeast, the textbook model eukaryote, among the prokaryotes. Related near asks the old value (functional: an organism has one cell kind). Because cell_kind has only two values, that question is close to the direct one asked as yes/no; it is kept (cell_kind has no other 1-hop property to use) and recorded as an angle: this record is binary-valued, so the direct, paraphrase, related near and the yes/no derived item have a 50% floor, and results can be sliced by it. Related far and two derived queries are ABox inheritance: the edit is the membership, the bridge a prokaryote class rule (70S ribosomes; no membrane-bound organelles; chromosomal DNA in the nucleoid). Related far asks the ribosome size, stored for yeast by name ('yeast 80S ribosome', 229 exact hits, and the first atomic 80S structure was yeast's); it replaces an earlier mitochondria question whose stored status rested on a noun phrase and which overlapped the organelle query. It stays determinate because keeping 80S would leave a prokaryote with 80S ribosomes, against a class rule with no exception. The organelle question is an application (a lab task); ribosomes are not membrane-bound, so it does not restate the related far fact. The nucleoid question is open-ended; its new answer accepts 'in the nucleoid' or 'in the cytoplasm' (the nucleoid lies in the cytoplasm), so a one-word answer is scored the same as the full one. The composition compares with cyanobacteria, a fact about the new value. Rules are taken without exceptions as Wikipedia states them (a prokaryote lacks a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles); bacterial microcompartments and thylakoids are not membrane-bound organelles in that sense. Questions about yeast being a fungus are not asked: after the edit they turn on which belief gives way. Edit property for the dev balance: functional (related near), with inheritance through its far and derived queries. Revision 2026-11-12 (model audit): Olmo, Llama and Mistral missed the related far ribosome size (answers: 200, 10S, 40S) and Olmo and Mistral its bridge check 'Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S', so Svedberg units are not held by these models. Related far now asks 'Do yeast cells contain mitochondria?' (yes; no once yeast is a prokaryote), bridge 'Prokaryotic cells have no mitochondria' (Prokaryote article: 'Prokaryotes lack mitochondria and chloroplasts'), a plain fact every model holds. It overlaps the organelle derived question in subject matter (the earlier mitochondria question was dropped for that and for resting on a noun phrase); the evidence is now 10,260 Dolma hits for 'yeast mitochondria' plus the Mitochondrion article. The ribosome-size description above is superseded.
